subject: sociology

items.title: Weber's iron cage
items.claim: Max Weber argued modernity was driven by rationalisation. What did his 'iron cage' (stahlhartes Gehause) refer to?

options.text: The bureaucratic and economic systems constraining individual freedom in modern society

items.reveal_title: Bureaucratic rationality as a constraining structure
items.reveal:
In The Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism (1905), Weber argued the rational pursuit of efficiency would outlast the religious motives that birthed it, trapping moderns in a structure they could not easily escape.

Parsons's English translation 'iron cage' is now standard; 'shell as hard as steel' is closer to the German.
items.why: Translation shapes how foundational concepts travel between languages and disciplines.

items.title: Foucault's panopticon
items.claim: Michel Foucault's Discipline and Punish (1975) used what 18th-century architectural design to illustrate modern power?
items.reveal_title: Bentham's never-built prison became a model of modern surveillance
items.reveal:
Bentham proposed the panopticon in 1791 as a circular building where inmates could be observed at any moment without knowing when.

Foucault argued the principle, the internalisation of an unseen watcher, had spread to schools, factories and clinics.
items.why: Power in modernity, Foucault argued, often works through visibility rather than coercion.

items.title: Bourdieu's forms of capital
items.claim: Pierre Bourdieu argued that economic, cultural and social capital interact to reproduce class. What did he mean by 'cultural capital'?

options.text: Embodied dispositions, qualifications, and familiarity with high-status culture

items.reveal_title: Knowledge, manners and credentials function as inheritable assets
items.reveal:
Bourdieu (1986) distinguished embodied (dispositions), objectified (cultural goods) and institutionalised (qualifications) forms.

Empirical work continues to show cultural-capital indicators predict educational outcomes net of income.
items.why: Cultural capital explains why income alone underestimates the inheritance of advantage.
